key_insight: For per-gate VQE optimization, Riemannian methods on U(2) showed no practical advantage over a well-tuned Euler-angle Adam baseline.
engineering_relevance: Optimizer choice alone is unlikely to improve VQE training unless benchmark design, parameterization, and validation are handled carefully.
method: Compared direct manifold optimization on each single-qubit gate in U(2) against Adam on an equivalent unconstrained Euler-angle chart.
Initialized both methods from the same unitaries and tuned learning rates separately.
Tested metric, retraction, and momentum transport variants to check robustness.
evidence_signal: On a validated hydrogen-chain benchmark, the two approaches were interleaved in final error and success rate, and the classical baseline was not slower in successful runs.
watch_item: Reported gains can be fabricated by subtle benchmark or implementation issues, including non-unitary retractions, projected-step baselines, trivial test cases, or learning-rate sweeps that only succeed at the grid boundary.
paper_title: A Controlled Null Result for Per-Gate Riemannian Optimization in VQE
